messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Contingency Tables
parts:
Not from within the GUI, but there is a function to convert a contingency table matrix to a data.frame.

Suppose you have a matrix named cont.matrix, as in the following

> cont.matrix <- matrix(c(4,5,10,4),ncol=2)
> cont.matrix
    [,1] [,2]
[1,]    4   10
[2,]    5    4

then you can convert it using the table.to.data function:

> dat <- table.to.data(cont.matrix)
> dat
  V1 V2
1   1  1
2   1  1
3   1  1
4   1  1
5   1  2
6   1  2
7   1  2
8   1  2
9   1  2
10  1  2
11  1  2
12  1  2
13  1  2
14  1  2
15  2  1
16  2  1
17  2  1
18  2  1
19  2  1
20  2  2
21  2  2
22  2  2
23  2  2

You should now have a data.frame named dat which you can analyze with the contingency table dialog:

> tables<-contingency.tables(
+ row.vars=d(V1),
+ col.vars=d(V2),data=dat)
> tables<-add.chi.squared(tables)
> print(tables,prop.r=T,prop.c=T,prop.t=F)
================================================================================

-----------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|

             Row %    |   28.571% |   71.429% |   60.870% |

-----------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
